---
title: "Categorical endpoints — `[binary_model]`"
---

Categorical (discrete-state) endpoints let a model score a **non-Gaussian**
observation — a category index rather than a continuous concentration. The first
member of the family is the **binary / Bernoulli** endpoint: mixed-effects
**logistic regression**, declared with a `[binary_model]` block.

> Ordinal (proportional-odds), Poisson, and negative-binomial endpoints are planned
> follow-ups in the same family. This page documents the binary endpoint only.

## The `[binary_model]` block

```ini
[binary_model]
cmt   = 3
logit = TH0 + THX * X + THT * TIME     ; log-odds of P(DV = 1)
; link = logit                          ; optional; logit is the default
```

Observations for the block's `cmt` carry `DV ∈ {0, 1}` (`EVID = 0`). The model
computes a per-observation probability (under the default logit link; see [The probit
link](#the-probit-link) for the other)

$$
p = \operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\eta_\text{lp}) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\eta_\text{lp}}},
$$

where the **linear predictor** `logit` (the log-odds) is any expression over the
same namespace the hazard and error blocks use — population parameters `θ`, random
effects `η`, data covariates, values from `[individual_parameters]`, and the
per-record `TIME` builtin. The data term is the negative Bernoulli log-likelihood

$$
-\log L = -\sum_j \big[\, y_j \log p_j + (1 - y_j)\log(1 - p_j) \,\big].
$$

### Keys

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|-----|----------|---------|
| `cmt`   | yes | Data-file `CMT` column value for this endpoint's rows. |
| `logit` | one of `logit` / `probit` | Linear predictor under the logit link (log-odds of `DV = 1`). Any θ/η/covariate/`[individual_parameters]`/`TIME` expression. |
| `probit` | one of `logit` / `probit` | The same linear predictor under the probit link (see [The probit link](#the-probit-link)). |
| `link`  | no  | `logit` (the default) or `probit`. It must agree with the predictor's key. |

### The probit link

Write the predictor under `probit =` instead of `logit =` and the model computes

$$
p = \Phi(\eta_\text{lp}),
$$

the standard-normal CDF of the linear predictor, which is NONMEM's `P = PHI(LP)` and R's
`glm(..., family = binomial(link = "probit"))`. `link = probit` may be added, but it is
implied by the key:

```ini
[binary_model]
cmt    = 3
probit = TH0 + THX * X + ETA_I        ; P(DV = 1) = Phi(...)
```

The key names the link, so a predictor is never called `logit` when it is not one. A
block with `link = probit` and a `logit =` predictor (or the other way round) is refused,
and so is a block that gives both keys. `cloglog` is not available.

The data term is the same Bernoulli likelihood, computed as `−log Φ(s·η_lp)` with
`s = +1` for `DV = 1` and `−1` for `DV = 0`. It is evaluated in log space and never forms
`Φ` itself, so a record far in either tail (an event at `η_lp = −40`, say) contributes its
exact `≈ η_lp²/2` rather than `log(0)`. The gradient, the η-Hessian and the covariance
step's derivatives are exact, as under logit.

The probit link is anchored against NONMEM `METHOD=COND LAPLACE LIKE` with `P = PHI(LP)`
on a 2400-row binary meta-analysis fixture (`probit_b1` in `nonmem_anchor/README.md`).

### Random effects and the fixed-effects special case

A per-subject random effect in the predictor (`logit = TH0 + ETA_I`) gives a
**mixed-effects** logistic model — a random intercept (or slope). Omitting all
random effects (no `omega`, `n_eta = 0`) gives ordinary **fixed-effects logistic
regression**, exactly analogous to base-R `glm(..., family = binomial)`. Both are
supported; the fixed-effects case needs no `[structural_model]`, `[error_model]`, or
`[individual_parameters]` blocks (a logistic-only model can be just `[parameters]` +
`[binary_model]` + `[fit_options]`).

Covariates on the predictor are read **per record**: the `TIME` builtin is the
record's time, and a covariate column that changes within a subject (an arm, a dose
group) is read at the record's own value, as a `$PRED` reads the current record (#2562).
The one exception is a subject that also carries time-to-event records, whose rows the
reader cannot line up one-to-one with its binary records: a time-varying covariate on
the predictor is then refused (`E_ENDPOINT_TV_COVARIATE`), since it could only be read
at baseline.

A θ level block (`theta PLACEBO[STUDY, TIME](0.0)`) may be read in the predictor, as in
a binary model-based meta-analysis: each record is scored at the level its own columns
name, and the binary records define the block's levels as Gaussian observations do (see
[θ level blocks](parameters.qmd)). It may also be `profile`d there, under either link
(see [Through a link](parameters.qmd#through-a-link)).

## Data format

`DV` holds the 0/1 outcome directly (there is no censoring code). One row per
observation; no dose rows are needed for a logistic-only model.

```csv
ID,TIME,DV,CMT,EVID,MDV,X
1,0,0,3,0,0,1.07
1,1,0,3,0,0,1.07
1,2,1,3,0,0,1.07
2,0,1,3,0,0,-1.01
```

A `DV` value of `2` or more on a binary CMT is a data error — the fit stops with a
clear message (an ordered response with more than two categories needs an ordinal
endpoint, which is not yet available).

## Example

`examples/binary_logistic.ferx` (with `data/binary_logistic.csv`) fits a
fixed-effects logistic model with a subject covariate `X` and a `TIME` effect:

```ini
[parameters]
  theta TH0(0.0, -10.0, 10.0)
  theta THX(0.0, -10.0, 10.0)
  theta THT(0.0, -10.0, 10.0)

[covariates]
  X continuous

[binary_model]
  cmt   = 3
  logit = TH0 + THX * X + THT * TIME
```

See [Categorical estimation](../estimation/categorical.qmd) for the estimator
guidance and the validation against R `glm`.
